species.summary: One of North America's largest birds, with a wingspan of about nine feet. Flocks soar over the Lahontan Valley on their way to feed in shallow wetlands.
id_tips: Huge white bird with a long orange bill and pouch
Black flight feathers show only when the wings are spread
Scoops fish while swimming; it does not plunge-dive
Often soars in slow, wheeling flocks high overhead
species.habitat: Shallow lakes, marshes and reservoirs with plenty of fish.
species.best_season: Spring through early fall (March to October)
species.where_to_find: Look over open water at Stillwater and on calm mornings at Soda Lake.

species.summary: An elegant shorebird that sweeps its upturned bill side to side through shallow water to catch tiny invertebrates.
id_tips: Long, thin bill that curves upward
Rusty-cinnamon head and neck in spring and summer
Bold black-and-white wings and long blue-gray legs
Feeds by swinging its bill through the water like a scythe
species.habitat: Shallow, open wetlands, mudflats and alkaline lake edges.
species.where_to_find: Scan the shallow edges at Stillwater, Carson Lake and Soda Lake.

photo.alt: Placeholder illustration of an American avocet wading in shallow water

model.alt: 3D model of an American avocet (stand-in duck model at avocet size)

species.summary: A dark, glossy wading bird that probes mud and flooded fields with a long, down-curved bill. The Lahontan Valley is one of its key nesting areas.
id_tips: Looks black at a distance; maroon with a green and bronze sheen up close
Thin white border around the face in breeding season
Flies in lines or loose V shapes with neck stretched out
species.habitat: Marshes, wet meadows and flooded farm fields.
species.where_to_find: Watch flooded fields around town and the marsh edges at Carson Lake and Stillwater.
